text:
Ryan: Noticed odd quota burns in APAC this morning. Spike correlates with many short WS reconnects that each bill a small token chunk.
Maya: Any client or shard pattern?
Ryan: Mostly eu + apac edge, many with the same user id but different upstream shards. Example trace (trimmed):```text
trace_id=tr_99 resume=res-42 client=203.0.113.5 upstream=10.10.1.4 event=reconnect billed=37
trace_id=tr_99 resume=res-42 client=203.0.113.5 upstream=10.10.2.9 event=reconnect billed=41
```So two reconnects within 2s hitting different upstreams.
Akash: Could be socket half-close. Edge forwarded PONG earlier than final close, router accepted resume on shard B while shard A also resumed -> double-meter.
Zoe: Is our resume id per-connection or per-session? If per-connection we can't dedupe across shards easily.
Laura: Resume is per-session (client generated). We rely on a global resume namespace for idempotency in meter. But meter keys are built from (route, resume_id) and our route normalization differs between router and meter.
meter-bot: FYI: recent deploy v2026.04.01-router changed route canonicalization to include zone suffix (route -> route.zone).
Maya: That explains it. Router emitting route=apac-1 and meter storing apac-1.a in some cases. Join queries in Console are using the old route tag, causing mismatch.
Akash: We should avoid relying on route for dedupe. Better to canonicalize resume id to a single global namespace (hash the resume + account id) and store a short dedupe key in the meter with TTL. Quick win: add global dedupe-index in Redis (or existing memstore) where meter checks recent resume hashes for 15s.
Ryan: Risk: extra roundtrip adds latency to meter path. Can we do local in-memory LRU per-metric-shard first, fall back to redis if uncertain?
Akash: Yes, implement a two-level dedupe: memcache LRU + redis fallback. Feature flag to roll out.
Zoe: UX: Console should surface "per-route vs per-resume" grouping so customers don't misinterpret shard splits as multiple sessions.
Laura: Also need a dashboard panel: duplicate_resume_rate by account and route. Add panel + a single alert when duplicate resume rate > 0.5% for 10m.
meter-bot: Suggested PromQL: `sum by (account,route)(rate(resume_reconnects_total[5m])) - sum by (account,route)(rate(resume_unique_reconnects_total[5m]))` -> use as numerator for duplicates.
Maya: Rollout: implement dedupe in meter (feature flag off), add route-normalizer change in router to keep old tag semantics (compat-mode) for 2w, then flip meter dedupe on in canary.
Ryan: For customer impact: we should send a short ops email to affected accounts with sample time windows and note we will credit obvious double-billed spikes.
Akash: Implementation notes: 1) Add resume_hash = sha256(account_id + resume_id) -> store 64-bit prefix as dedupe key. 2) Memcache store per-meter-worker with TTL 15s. 3) Redis shared store for cross-worker dedupe during canary. 4) Flag `meter_dedupe_v2`.
Zoe: Also, investigate PONG handling at edge. If we accept PONG as keepalive but client closed shortly after, we might create a race where both old and new connections can resume. We need a short grace window per-socket before allowing resume on another shard.
Maya: Could we attach a short socket fence token on resume succeed that is checked for a 3s window? If another resume arrives with same resume_id but no fence token, reject as duplicate.
Ryan: That might be brittle across proxies. Prefer dedupe in meter + route-normalizer immediate fixes. Edge fix as follow-up.
Laura: Action list: Akash -> implement two-level dedupe and feature flag. Maya -> add console panel and alert + ops note draft. Ryan -> coordinate billing credits and oncall pager rule for large deltas. Zoe -> open edge PONG race issue and add logs for resume fencing.
Akash: Starting a canary of `meter-dedupe-v2` in apac on 5% traffic. Will post link to canary metrics shortly.
Maya: If we see duplicate_resume_rate drop to near zero in canary, plan 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 8 hours with kill-switch.
Ryan: Thanks. Keep updates here and tag #oncall if any paging thresholds hit.
meter-bot: Canary started: meter-dedupe-v2 -> 5% apac, watch `resume_dedupe_miss` and `duplicate_resume_rate`.
